children: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (NSE:HAL) enters FY27 with a Rs 2.54 trillion order book and ambitious expansion plans—from scaling AL-31FP and Shakti engine lines to boosting LCA and rotorcraft production—while targeting double‑digit growth and 30–31% EBITDA amid supply risks tied to foreign engines and concentration on one major customer.
Previous Week Recap
HAL Orders Growth Target
: HAL starts FY27 with Rs 2.54 trillion order book and targets Rs 90,000 crore more in two years, citing contracts like 143 ALHs, Su-30 upgrades and 40 Dornier modernizations.
HAL Seeks Double-Digit Revenue
: HAL targets double-digit revenue growth in FY26–FY27 and aims to sustain 30–31% EBITDA margin, citing net-debt free balance sheet and strong internal cash generation.
HAL Traders: Execution Risks
: HAL traders: execution risks include delays from foreign-sourced critical parts, possible GE engine delivery issues, and revenue concentration from reliance on one major customer.
HAL Invests To Boost Output
: HAL to invest Rs335 crore to boost AL-31FP output from 30 to 50 units, indigenise materials with MIDHANI; govt funds second Shakti line aiming 100 engines/year by 2028–29.
HAL Expands Capacity At Bengaluru, Nashik
: HAL to expand Bengaluru and Nashik capacity to boost LCA and HTT-40 output; Bengaluru and Tumakuru to prioritize LCH production to meet delivery schedules.
LCA Mk1A Output Depends On GE
: HAL says LCA Mk1A output hinges on steady GE engine supply. Indian Air Force ordered 180 Mk1A jets; HAL’s production readiness tied to GE engine deliveries scheduled through 2026.
Koraput Shakti Engine Milestone
: HAL Koraput delivered its 2,000th Shakti helicopter engine; division has overhauled 9,000+ engines. HAL announced a second Shakti production line at Koraput with Rs 218 crore investment.
Motilal Oswal: HAL Revenue Rise
: Motilal Oswal sees HAL Q2 revenue up ~14% YoY and margins rising 100 bps to 24.5%, driven by LCA Mk1 and other deliveries; Tejas Mk1A deliveries noted as a key trigger.
HAL-GE Penalties For Delays
: HAL and GE Aviation have contractual penalty clauses for delays in F404 engine deliveries, including liquidated damages, aimed at enforcing supplier timelines for the Tejas program.
Defence Minister Urges Koraput Hub

: Defence Minister urged Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) to expand Koraput into an aerospace propulsion hub by nurturing suppliers, mentoring MSMEs and start-ups, and linking academia and industry.
